text: Barclays Home Contact us Log in Menu Multi-asset portfolio allocation MULTI-ASSET PORTFOLIO ALLOCATION 2 February 2026 Julien Lafargue, London UK, Chief Market Strategist Share page via Facebook Share page via X Share page via LinkedIn Share page via email Barclays Private Bank discusses asset allocation views within the context of a multi-asset class portfolio. Our views elsewhere in the publication are absolute and within the context of each asset class. Summary Equity markets began 2026 by setting fresh highs, led by small caps and stocks with high momentum. Meanwhile, last year’s geopolitical and policy uncertainty has stretched into this one. During January, we tilted portfolios towards an overweight in emerging market equities, where we see opportunities for growth to surprise on the upside and for the asset class to outperform in a lower interest rate and possibly weaker US dollar environment. As such, emerging market equities look better value to us than US peers. Within allocations, there is a strong argument for more diversification to mitigate policy uncertainty. Opportunities are popping up in unloved parts of the market that offer more attractive valuations, without sacrificing quality. We continue to seek the right balance between conviction and diversification, including across geographies. With bond markets still facing higher rates and lower credit spreads than their multi-year ranges, we allocate more to developed government bonds while being more selective in investment grade and high yield credit. Cash and short duration bonds Cash and short duration bond allocations were cut to neutral in January to fund an increase in exposure to emerging market equities. Fixed income Divergence in the key economies of the US, China and the EU is driving different growth and inflation trade-offs for their respective central banks. Core rates are expected to be a helpful diversifier from risk-asset exposure in the event of a weaker economy − and so portfolios are invested up to the strategic allocation. Those different growth and inflation dynamics can be reflected through curve and duration positioning within the asset class. Credit spreads remain historically tight, albeit offering attractive carry in terms of total yield.  Selection is key, as spreads have scope to widen in an adverse scenario. In high yield and emerging markets, we prefer the trade-off between credit spreads and quality in emerging markets and initiated a small overweight at the start of the year, funded from investment grade credit allocations. Equities Developed market equity exposure has been managed down to the neutral level since October in response to the momentum-led and concentrated run up in US large-cap stocks. Exposure to emerging market equities was increased in October and again in January, taking them to an overweight position. This broadens and diversifies equity exposure in response to the increasingly narrow US leadership. In line with our long-term investment philosophy, portfolios are geared towards high-quality, cash-generative and conservatively capitalised businesses. Alternative trading strategies (ATS) The higher rate environment means there is a higher opportunity cost for ATS, so the allocation remains at a lower strategic level. Our focus is on strategies that offer low correlations to equity markets − providing diversification benefits. Commodities Despite the gold price continuing to hit record levels in 2026, as a risk-mitigating asset and diversifier from the US dollar, the yellow metal is our preferred direct commodity exposure. Elsewhere, we believe that our risk budget is better spent outside of the asset class.
